{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash -ex
#FLUX -N 1
# NOTE: SLURM's -w (--nodelist) forces a job to run on a specific node. The Flux
# equivalent is to use a hostname constraint.
#FLUX -C hostname:voltron
#FLUX -J linear-faults-quant
#FLUX --exclusive
#FLUX -t 48:00:00
#FLUX -o {name}.{id}.out

# NOTE: This job requires a GPU, as indicated by loading the CUDA module and
# interacting with NVIDIA kernel modules. A GPU should be explicitly requested
# to ensure correct scheduling, e.g., #FLUX --gpus=1

export IGNORE_CC_MISMATCH=1
ITERS=1

module load cuda

sudo modprobe nvidia-uvm #uvm_perf_prefetch_enable=0 #uvm_perf_fault_coalesce=0 #uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=1
sudo rmmod -f nvidia-uvm
sudo modprobe nvidia-uvm uvm_perf_prefetch_enable=0 #uvm_perf_fault_coalesce=0 #uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=1

cd ../../tools/syslogger/
make
cd -

bsizes=(256)
#bsizes=(32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 6144)
#bsizes=(32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 6144)

psizes=()
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    for ((i=1; i<$#+1;i++));do
        psizes+=(${i})
    done
else
    psizes=(1048576 8388608)
    #for ((i=2**0; $i < 2**24; i=$i * 2)) do ## should be 0-20 12 - 33
        #psizes+=(${i})
    #done
fi

cd ../linear
make

rm -f quant*.csv
find . -maxdepth 1  -name 'log_*' -type d -exec rm -rf {} +

cd ../../drivers/x86_64-460.27.04/batchd/kernel
    
make -j
sudo make modules_install
cd -
# prefetching on or off
#for ((pf=0; pf < 1; pf++)); do
for ((pf=0; pf < 2; pf++)); do
    # iter batch sizes
    for ((k=0; k<${#bsizes[@]}; k++)); do
        bsize=${bsizes[$k]}
        # iter problem size
        for ((i=0;i<${#psizes[@]}; i++)); do
            psize=${psizes[$i]}
            if [ $pf -eq 1 ]; then
                logdir="log_pf_${psize}_bsize_${bsizes[$k]}"
            else 
                logdir="log_${psize}_bsize_${bsizes[$k]}"
            fi
            mkdir -p $logdir

            # if want more than one sample per problem size
            for ((j=0;j<$ITERS;j++)); do
                sudo dmesg -C
                sudo rmmod -f nvidia-uvm
                sudo modprobe nvidia-uvm uvm_perf_prefetch_enable=${pf} uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=${bsizes[$k]}   #uvm_perf_fault_coalesce=0 #uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=1
                if [ $pf -eq 1 ]; then
                    out="quant-pf-${bsize}.csv"
                else
                    out="quant-${bsize}.csv"
                fi
                echo "size,$psize" >> $out 

                file=linear_$j
                logfile=/scratch1/$file
                pwd
                
                make clean
                make DEFS=-DPNUM=$psize


                ../../tools/syslogger/log "$logfile" &
                pid=$!
                sleep 8

                echo "pid: $pid"
                time ./page | grep "alloced,\|perf," >> $out

                len=`cat "$logfile" | wc -l`
                sleep 5
                until [ $(expr $(cat "$logfile" | wc -l)  - ${len}) -eq 0 ]; do
                    len=`cat "$logfile" | wc -l`
                    sleep 3
                done
                sleep 1
                kill $pid
                mv $logfile $logdir/
                ../../tools/sys2csv/log2csv.sh $logdir/$file
                dmesg > $logdir/dmesg_$i
            done
        done
    done
done

cd -




sudo rmmod nvidia-uvm
sudo modprobe nvidia-uvm #uvm_perf_prefetch_enable=0 uvm_perf_fault_coalesce=0 #uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=1
"
}

issues: The script is critically missing a GPU resource request. The code loads the `cuda` module and repeatedly uses `sudo` to manipulate the `nvidia-uvm` kernel module, which are clear indicators that a GPU is required. Without a directive like `#FLUX --gpus=1`, the job may be scheduled on a CPU-only node where it will immediately fail. This is the most significant issue with the job specification.

The use of `sudo` within a batch script is a major security concern and is not permitted in most shared HPC environments. This script requires root-level permissions to modify kernel modules, which is not typical for a user job and makes the script non-portable and likely to fail due to insufficient permissions.

The directive '#FLUX -C hostname:voltron' hardcodes the job to a single, specific node ('voltron'). This is an anti-pattern in shared computing environments as it prevents the scheduler from flexibly placing the job on any available node that meets the requirements. If 'voltron' is busy, offline, or removed from the cluster, the job will fail to run or remain queued indefinitely. It is better to request generic features (e.g., `-C gpu`) and let the scheduler find a suitable node.

cd -

bsizes=(256)
#bsizes=(32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 6144)
#bsizes=(32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 6144)

psizes=()
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    for ((i=1; i<$#+1;i++));do
        psizes+=(${i})
    done
else
    psizes=(1048576 8388608)
    #for ((i=2**0; $i < 2**24; i=$i * 2)) do ## should be 0-20 12 - 33
        #psizes+=(${i})
    #done
fi

cd ../linear
make

rm -f quant*.csv
find . -maxdepth 1  -name 'log_*' -type d -exec rm -rf {} +

cd ../../drivers/x86_64-460.27.04/batchd/kernel
    
make -j
sudo make modules_install
cd -
# prefetching on or off
#for ((pf=0; pf < 1; pf++)); do
for ((pf=0; pf < 2; pf++)); do
    # iter batch sizes
    for ((k=0; k<${#bsizes[@]}; k++)); do
        bsize=${bsizes[$k]}
        # iter problem size
        for ((i=0;i<${#psizes[@]}; i++)); do
            psize=${psizes[$i]}
            if [ $pf -eq 1 ]; then
                logdir="log_pf_${psize}_bsize_${bsizes[$k]}"
            else 
                logdir="log_${psize}_bsize_${bsizes[$k]}"
            fi
            mkdir -p $logdir

            # if want more than one sample per problem size
            for ((j=0;j<$ITERS;j++)); do
                sudo dmesg -C
                sudo rmmod -f nvidia-uvm
                sudo modprobe nvidia-uvm uvm_perf_prefetch_enable=${pf} uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=${bsizes[$k]}   #uvm_perf_fault_coalesce=0 #uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=1
                if [ $pf -eq 1 ]; then
                    out="quant-pf-${bsize}.csv"
                else
                    out="quant-${bsize}.csv"
                fi
                echo "size,$psize" >> $out 

                file=linear_$j
                logfile=/scratch1/$file
                pwd
                
                make clean
                make DEFS=-DPNUM=$psize


                ../../tools/syslogger/log "$logfile" &
                pid=$!
                sleep 8

                echo "pid: $pid"
                time ./page | grep "alloced,\|perf," >> $out

                len=`cat "$logfile" | wc -l`
                sleep 5
                until [ $(expr $(cat "$logfile" | wc -l)  - ${len}) -eq 0 ]; do
                    len=`cat "$logfile" | wc -l`
                    sleep 3
                done
                sleep 1
                kill $pid
                mv $logfile $logdir/
                ../../tools/sys2csv/log2csv.sh $logdir/$file
                dmesg > $logdir/dmesg_$i
            done
        done
    done
done

cd -




sudo rmmod nvidia-uvm
sudo modprobe nvidia-uvm #uvm_perf_prefetch_enable=0 uvm_perf_fault_coalesce=0 #uvm_perf_fault_batch_count=1
